section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: BASIC files are tokenised when stored as file type BASIC (&hex;FFB). Usually the tokenisation process it performed by the BASIC module. However, this isn't always possible - for example, if the process is being run on a non-RISC OS system. The *BASICTokenise tool can be used to convert untokenised BASIC Text (filetype &hex;FD1) to Tokenised BASIC.

command-definition.name: BASICTokenise
command-definition.description: Convert a BASIC Text file to tokenised BASIC file
command-definition.parameter: filename of the text file to read
filename of the tokenised BASIC file to write to

use.p: This command is used to tokenise a textual BASIC program. *BASICTokenise will process the text file to produce a BASIC file.
The tool is only capable of tokenising BASIC files with and without line numbers present, using the tokens supported by the BASIC V dialect of BBC BASIC.

Lines may be given prefix numbers which will be used as the line number. Lines will not be reordered if they are given out of sequence. Lines without prefix numbers will be numbered from line 10 in steps of 10.

revision.author: Gerph
revision.title: Added notes about supported features
revision.change: We don't support line number references, and lines won't be reordered.

revision.author: Gerph
revision.title: Line number references
revision.change: Line number references, eg 'GOTO' and 'GOSUB' are now supported.
